plan.contextChunk: This figure sets three side-by-side panels, (a), (b), and (c), showing one small undirected graph and two ways of storing it. Panel (a) draws the graph as five gray circles numbered 1 through 5, with 1 at the upper left, 2 at the upper right, 3 at the far right, 4 at the lower middle, and 5 at the lower left, joined by seven straight edges: 1-2, 1-5, 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4, and 4-5. Panel (b) gives the adjacency-list form as a vertical array of five gray cells indexed 1 to 5, each holding a pointer arrow into a horizontal chain of two-field records whose right field is either an arrow onward or a diagonal slash marking the end. Row 1 chains 2 then 5; row 2 chains 1, 5, 3, 4; row 3 chains 2 then 4; row 4 chains 2, 5, 3; row 5 chains 4, 1, 2. Panel (c) gives the adjacency matrix as a bordered five-by-five grid of zeros and ones with rows and columns both headed 1 through 5, zeros along the diagonal and entries symmetric across it. Laying the picture beside the two tables lets a single edge be found three ways, and it makes plain that each undirected edge is stored twice.

interactionPlan.concept: A single undirected graph can be stored as a drawing, an adjacency list, or an adjacency matrix, and every undirected edge is recorded twice — as two list records and as two symmetric 1s in the matrix.

Panel (a): seven straight edges 1-2, 1-5, 2-5, 2-3, 2-4, 3-4, 4-5
Panel (b): vertical index array of five gray cells labeled 1..5
Panel (b): pointer arrow from each index cell into its record chain
Panel (b): two-field record boxes (value | next-pointer) forming chains: row1 = 2→5→/, row2 = 1→5→3→4→/, row3 = 2→4→/, row4 = 2→5→3→/, row5 = 4→1→2→/
Panel (b): diagonal slash marking the null next-pointer at each chain end
Panel (c): bordered 5x5 grid with column headers 1..5 on top and row headers 1..5 on left
Panel (c): 0/1 entries — row1 0 1 0 0 1; row2 1 0 1 1 1; row3 0 1 0 1 0; row4 0 1 1 0 1; row5 1 1 0 1 0 (zero diagonal, symmetric)
Panel captions (a), (b), (c) beneath each panel

demo_steps.title: One graph, three encodings
demo_steps.narration: The same five-vertex graph appears as a drawing, an adjacency list, and an adjacency matrix. With focus on the graph, pick vertex 2 and watch its neighbors (1, 3, 4, 5) highlight in the list row and the matrix row/column.

demo_steps.title: An edge is stored twice
demo_steps.narration: Click edge 2-5 in the drawing (or the 1 at row 2, column 5). The two list records — 5 in row 2's chain and 2 in row 5's chain — and the symmetric matrix cells (2,5) and (5,2) all light up together.

demo_steps.title: Same relationships, matrix view
demo_steps.narration: Switch focus to the matrix. Selecting any vertex now highlights its full row and column, and the symmetry across the diagonal is exactly the list's duplicated records seen from another angle.

demo_steps.title: Add an edge
demo_steps.narration: Choose the non-adjacent pair 1-3 and press add edge. A new line 1-3 appears in the graph, a record 3 is prepended to row 1's chain and a record 1 to row 3's chain, and matrix cells (1,3) and (3,1) flip from 0 to 1.

demo_steps.title: Remove an edge
demo_steps.narration: Now remove edge 3-4. The graph line vanishes, the record 4 leaves row 3's chain and 3 leaves row 4's chain, and matrix cells (3,4) and (4,3) flip back to 0 — one logical change, four physical edits.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The three panels are the same graph, and the price of an undirected edge is duplication: it lives as two list records and two symmetric matrix 1s, so any edit must touch both copies.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Lay out three panels left-to-right with captions (a), (b), (c). Panel (a): light-gray filled circles with black outlines and centered numerals, thin black straight edges. Panel (b): a narrow gray index column on the left, each cell emitting a right arrow into a horizontal chain of two-compartment boxes (left = neighbor number, right = next arrow or a diagonal slash for null); keep chains left-aligned and vertically aligned with their index. Panel (c): a single bordered square grid, headers 1..5 above columns and left of rows, monospace 0/1 cells, zero diagonal. Use one consistent accent color (e.g. orange fill/outline) for all highlight states so a selected edge reads as the same object across the three panels; cross-fade highlights when the focus toggle changes rather than redrawing abruptly.

authoredContext: The adjacency-list representation of a graph G D .V; E/ consists of an array Adj of jV j lists, one for each vertex in V . For each u 2 V , the adjacency list AdjŒu contains all the vertices _x0017_ such that there is an edge .u; _x0017_/ 2 E. That is, AdjŒu consists of all the vertices adjacent to u in G. (Alternatively, it may contain pointers to these vertices.) Since the adjacency lists represent the edges of a graph, in pseudocode we treat the array Adj as an attribute of the graph, just as we treat the edge set E. In pseudocode, therefore, we will see notation such as G:AdjŒu. Figure 22.1(b) is an adjacency-list representation of the undirected graph in Figure 22.1(a).

discrepancies: Adjacency-list chain order differs from the source for two rows: source row 4 is 2→5→3 and row 5 is 4→1→2, but the generated buildAdjList() yields row 4 = 2→3→5 and row 5 = 1→2→4 (insertion order follows the edge array, not the textbook order).

The 'Focus' dropdown (Graph / Adjacency list / Adjacency matrix) is non-functional: setFocus() only stores a variable and clears highlights, so selecting a representation produces no visible change in the figure, contradicting the narration that says 'With focus on the graph…'.

The provided rendered screenshot shows a completely empty drawing area (no graph, list, or matrix visible) at the captured viewport; the deterministic verifier reports a visible root, so this is treated as a capture/aspect-ratio concern rather than a scored failure, but it means the default state could not be visually confirmed as a drop-in replacement.
Source is strictly grayscale; the generated figure introduces an orange accent color for highlights (an acceptable interactive enhancement, but a deviation from the static source's palette).
evaluation.notes: The code faithfully reconstructs all three panels (5-vertex graph with the correct 7 edges, doubly-linked adjacency list with null slashes, and a symmetric 0/1 adjacency matrix with 1–5 headers) and provides genuinely meaningful cross-representation highlighting plus add/remove-edge editing and a 5-step demo, but the Focus dropdown does nothing visible, two adjacency-list rows are ordered differently from the textbook, and the captured screenshot shows a blank canvas so the static default could not be visually verified.
action_items: Make the Focus dropdown drive a real visual change (e.g., dim or de-emphasize the two non-focused panels, or scale/translate the viewbox to the selected panel); otherwise remove the control so no non-functional UI remains.
Order each adjacency-list chain to match the source exactly (row 4: 2,5,3; row 5: 4,1,2) instead of relying on edge-array insertion order.

Guarantee the SVG is visible at inline size: the 960×360 viewBox vertically centered in a tall container left the captured screenshot blank — set a sensible preserveAspectRatio/min-height or an aspect ratio closer to the docked container so all three panels render without depending on vertical centering.
Bump the list/matrix font sizes (currently 12–14 in a 960-wide viewBox) so values stay comfortably legible after the viewBox is scaled down to inline width.

⚠ Figure failed to load

discrepancies: The null/nil terminator in each adjacency-list chain is drawn as a backslash '\' (top-left to bottom-right) whereas the source uses a forward slash '/' (bottom-left to top-right).

Panel (c) draws a full internal cell grid (light gray lines between every row/column); the source matrix shows only a single outer rectangular border with the numerals spaced in a grid and no internal lines.

At init the step label reads '1/5' but applyStep(0) is never called, so step 1's vertex-2 cross-highlight and its narration are not actually shown until the user navigates away and back — the default state and the '1/5' label are slightly inconsistent.
evaluation.notes: The three-panel composition, the exact 5-vertex edge set, the adjacency-list chain ordering, and the 5x5 matrix values all match the source precisely, and the cross-representation highlighting plus add/remove-edge propagation are an excellent, concept-correct teaching interaction; only minor visual deviations remain (backslash vs slash nil marker, added internal matrix gridlines, and an init step that skips step 1's highlight).
action_items: Draw the nil terminator as a forward slash '/' by reversing the diagonal (line from rx+recW-6,ry+recH-6 to divX+6,ry+6) so it matches the source's pointer-null glyph.
Drop the per-cell internal gridlines in drawMatrixPanel (keep only the outer n*cellS border and the spaced numerals) to match the source's border-only adjacency matrix.
Call applyStep(0) during initialization (instead of only drawAll + manual label set) so the displayed '1/5' step, its narration, and its vertex-2 highlight are all consistent on first paint.

feedback.rationale: Scores are consistently high (4-5), no failure modes are identified, concept accuracy is perfect, and the remaining discrepancies are trivial cosmetic details (slash direction, gridlines, init call) that do not meaningfully impact understanding or usability.
